quests.hint: Talking back and forth with someone to reach a deal both sides can accept.
quests.explanation: 'Negotiate a price' or 'negotiate a deal' are the phrases to remember. The noun form is 'negotiation.'
quests.textToSpeak: They had to ___ the price carefully before they could agree on a final deal.
quests.correctAnswer: They had to negotiate the price carefully before they could agree on a final deal.

quests.hint: Each side giving up a little to reach an agreement.
quests.explanation: 'Reach a compromise' works as a noun; 'to compromise' is the verb, meaning both people meet somewhere in the middle.
quests.textToSpeak: Both sides had to ___ in order to reach an agreement everyone was satisfied with.
quests.correctAnswer: Both sides had to compromise in order to reach an agreement everyone was satisfied with.

quests.hint: A formal written plan submitted for others to consider and approve.
quests.explanation: 'Submit a proposal' and 'write a proposal' are the ones you'll hear most. It can also mean asking someone to marry you, in a different context.
quests.textToSpeak: She wrote a detailed ___ outlining the new strategy and submitted it to the board.
quests.correctAnswer: She wrote a detailed proposal outlining the new strategy and submitted it to the board.

quests.hint: Working from home instead of commuting to an office.
quests.explanation: 'Remote working' or 'work remotely' both describe this setup. The word can also describe a distant, faraway place, in a different sense.
quests.textToSpeak: Many companies now offer ___ working options to attract and retain good staff.
quests.correctAnswer: Many companies now offer remote working options to attract and retain good staff.

quests.hint: The part of the day when roads are busiest with commuters.
quests.explanation: Rush hour is always singular, even though it usually lasts more than sixty minutes! 'During rush hour' is the phrase you'll use most.
quests.textToSpeak: Try to avoid driving during ___ - the traffic is absolutely gridlocked both ways.
quests.correctAnswer: Try to avoid driving during rush hour - the traffic is absolutely gridlocked both ways.

quests.hint: The overall mood or feeling of a place.
quests.explanation: 'A cosy atmosphere' or 'a tense atmosphere' describe very different moods. The same word also means the layer of gases around the Earth.
quests.textToSpeak: The restaurant had a wonderful ___ - intimate lighting and very friendly service.
quests.correctAnswer: The restaurant had a wonderful atmosphere - intimate lighting and very friendly service.

quests.hint: A style of cooking typical of a particular country or region.
quests.explanation: 'Local cuisine' and 'Italian cuisine' both sound natural here. It's a slightly more formal word than simply 'food.'
quests.textToSpeak: She loves exploring new places and always enjoys trying the local ___.
quests.correctAnswer: She loves exploring new places and always enjoys trying the local cuisine.

quests.hint: Comments and opinions given to help someone improve.
quests.explanation: Feedback is uncountable — say 'some feedback' or 'a piece of feedback,' never 'a feedback.'
quests.textToSpeak: She asked her manager for constructive ___ on how to improve her presentation skills.
quests.correctAnswer: She asked her manager for constructive feedback on how to improve her presentation skills.

quests.hint: A talk given to explain or share information with an audience.
quests.explanation: 'Give a presentation' and 'deliver a presentation' are the everyday way to say it. 'PowerPoint presentation' is a very common modern example.
quests.textToSpeak: He practised his ___ more than twenty times before delivering it to the board.
quests.correctAnswer: He practised his presentation more than twenty times before delivering it to the board.

quests.hint: Someone who doesn't eat meat or fish.
quests.explanation: 'Vegetarian options' is common on menus. It differs from 'vegan,' who avoids all animal products, including dairy and eggs.
quests.textToSpeak: She asked the waiter whether there were ___ options available on the menu.
quests.correctAnswer: She asked the waiter whether there were vegetarian options available on the menu.

quests.hint: The teaching provided by a school or university, or the fee paid for it.
quests.explanation: 'Tuition fees' is the standard British phrase for the cost of studying. Americans often just say 'tuition' alone to mean the same cost.
quests.textToSpeak: The university offers reduced ___ fees for students from lower-income backgrounds.
quests.correctAnswer: The university offers reduced tuition fees for students from lower-income backgrounds.

quests.hint: Money awarded to a student to help pay for their studies, based on merit or need.
quests.explanation: 'Win a scholarship' and 'a full scholarship' are worth learning together. 'Full' means it covers all the costs.
quests.textToSpeak: She won a full ___ to study at a prestigious university in the United States.
quests.correctAnswer: She won a full scholarship to study at a prestigious university in the United States.

quests.hint: Finishing a degree and officially completing your studies.
quests.explanation: 'Graduate from' a university is the phrase to remember. As a noun, 'a graduate' is the person who has finished.
quests.textToSpeak: He plans to ___ from university next summer and then travel for a year.
quests.correctAnswer: He plans to graduate from university next summer and then travel for a year.

quests.hint: Jittery and on edge before something important happens.
quests.explanation: 'Nervous about' or 'nervous before' both work. 'Nerves' is the plural noun form — 'she had a bad case of nerves.'
quests.textToSpeak: She felt incredibly ___ before stepping onto the stage for the very first time.
quests.correctAnswer: She felt incredibly nervous before stepping onto the stage for the very first time.

quests.hint: Sure of yourself and your abilities, without excessive doubt.
quests.explanation: 'Confident about' or 'confident in' both work, depending on what follows. The noun form is 'confidence.'
quests.textToSpeak: After months of practice, he felt much more ___ about speaking in public.
quests.correctAnswer: After months of practice, he felt much more confident about speaking in public.

quests.hint: The feeling right after worry disappears and everything turns out fine.
quests.explanation: 'Relieved to hear' or 'relieved that' both work. The noun form is 'relief' — 'a huge sense of relief.'
quests.textToSpeak: She was absolutely ___ when the doctor told her the test results were normal.
quests.correctAnswer: She was absolutely relieved when the doctor told her the test results were normal.

quests.hint: The sequence of events that make up a story.
quests.explanation: 'A complex plot' or 'follow the plot' are the go-to phrases. 'Plot twist' describes a surprising turn in the story.
quests.textToSpeak: The ___ of the thriller was so complex that she had to watch it twice.
quests.correctAnswer: The plot of the thriller was so complex that she had to watch it twice.

quests.hint: Written opinions, usually from critics, about a film, book, or product.
quests.explanation: 'Glowing reviews' means very positive ones. The word is often plural when talking about overall critical reception.
quests.textToSpeak: The film received glowing ___ from critics who praised its originality.
quests.correctAnswer: The film received glowing reviews from critics who praised its originality.

quests.hint: A long-term loan specifically used to buy a house.
quests.explanation: 'Take out a mortgage' is how most speakers say it. 'Pay off a mortgage' means finishing all the repayments, often after many years.
quests.textToSpeak: They took out a twenty-five-year ___ to buy their first family home.
quests.correctAnswer: They took out a twenty-five-year mortgage to buy their first family home.

quests.hint: Money borrowed that must eventually be paid back, often with interest.
quests.explanation: 'Apply for a loan' and 'take out a loan' both work. 'Student loan' is one of the most common types people mention.
quests.textToSpeak: She applied for a student ___ to cover the cost of her university tuition fees.
quests.correctAnswer: She applied for a student loan to cover the cost of her university tuition fees.

quests.hint: Money put into something with the hope it will grow in value.
quests.explanation: 'Make an investment' is the natural choice here. The verb form is 'invest' — 'she invested in company shares.'
quests.textToSpeak: He made a wise ___ in company shares that paid off significantly over five years.
quests.correctAnswer: He made a wise investment in company shares that paid off significantly over five years.

quests.hint: A doctor's official identification of what illness you have.
quests.explanation: 'Receive a diagnosis' or 'confirm a diagnosis' are how most speakers actually say it. The verb form is 'diagnose' — 'the doctor diagnosed the illness.'
quests.textToSpeak: The doctor explained the ___ carefully and outlined the available treatment options.
quests.correctAnswer: The doctor explained the diagnosis carefully and outlined the available treatment options.

quests.hint: The medical care given to help someone recover from an illness.
quests.explanation: 'A course of treatment' means a planned series of sessions. 'Undergo treatment' is a formal way to describe receiving it.
quests.textToSpeak: She began a six-month course of ___ that the specialist said was very effective.
quests.correctAnswer: She began a six-month course of treatment that the specialist said was very effective.

quests.hint: A doctor with expert knowledge in one particular area of medicine.
quests.explanation: 'Refer to a specialist' is what a general doctor does when a case needs expert attention. 'Specialise in' shows their specific area.
quests.textToSpeak: Her GP referred her to a ___ for a more detailed and thorough examination.
quests.correctAnswer: Her GP referred her to a specialist for a more detailed and thorough examination.

quests.hint: The yearly marker of an important date, like a wedding.
quests.explanation: 'Wedding anniversary' is the most common use. 'Twentieth anniversary' shows exactly how many years have passed.
quests.textToSpeak: They celebrated their twentieth wedding ___ with a wonderful trip to Rome.
quests.correctAnswer: They celebrated their twentieth wedding anniversary with a wonderful trip to Rome.

quests.hint: The formal agreement to get married, before the wedding itself.
quests.explanation: 'Announce an engagement' is the version people actually use. 'Engagement ring' is the piece of jewellery that usually comes with it.
quests.textToSpeak: She announced her ___ to her family over a special celebratory dinner.
quests.correctAnswer: She announced her engagement to her family over a special celebratory dinner.

quests.hint: A particular event, especially a special or memorable one.
quests.explanation: 'A special occasion' is the phrase you'll hear constantly. 'On this occasion' is a more formal way of saying 'this time.'
quests.textToSpeak: It was a truly special ___ that everyone present would long remember.
quests.correctAnswer: It was a truly special occasion that everyone present would long remember.

quests.hint: Giving money, time, or goods to help a good cause.
quests.explanation: 'Donate to' a charity is the one to remember. The noun form is 'donation' — 'she made a generous donation.'
quests.textToSpeak: She decided to ___ a portion of her bonus to a local children's charity.
quests.correctAnswer: She decided to donate a portion of her bonus to a local children's charity.

quests.hint: An event organised specifically to collect money for a cause.
quests.explanation: 'Hold a fundraiser' or 'organise a fundraiser' are the key expressions here. It combines 'fund' (money) and 'raise' (collect).
quests.textToSpeak: The school held a ___ to raise money for the new sports and arts facility.
quests.correctAnswer: The school held a fundraiser to raise money for the new sports and arts facility.

quests.hint: An organisation set up to help people or causes in need.
quests.explanation: 'Volunteer for a charity' or 'donate to charity' (without 'a') are both common. 'Charitable' is the adjective form.
quests.textToSpeak: He volunteers for a ___ that provides hot meals for homeless people in winter.
quests.correctAnswer: He volunteers for a charity that provides hot meals for homeless people in winter.
